items.title: The Leviathan That Knows Your Name

speakers.name: Captain Mara Vey
speakers.comment: Oxygen at forty-one percent. You are not cruel. I have checked. Cruelty would be something I could push against. You simply wait, and I have run out of ways to describe that. Thirty-nine.

speakers.name: The Leviathan That Knows Your Name
speakers.comment: Thirty-nine. I will still be here at nought. That is not a threat, small warm thing, it is arithmetic, and I have never once needed to hurry it. Say your name again. I like the way you say it.

speakers.name: Old Penny
speakers.comment: You have planned it perfect, and perfect is the tell. A thing that looks new is only a lie in good clothes. You want a job that looks like it has been sitting there a while.

speakers.name: Saint
speakers.comment: That is the note I did not have. Everything I build is too clean. Fine. I will age it. And no — nobody has called me kid in eleven years and I am not making it a thing now.

speakers.name: Margaux Dell
speakers.comment: You are the fun one right up to the alarm and then you are the fastest one, which nobody clocks because they are busy enjoying you. Keep doing that. Best cover in the crew and it is free.

speakers.name: Switch
speakers.comment: It is not cover, it is a personality, and I will thank you to — okay, no. It is cover. Damn. You do that thing where the sentence does two jobs. I hate it. Teach me.

speakers.name: Detective Aria Voss
speakers.comment: Most ordinary person in the room. That is what I wrote down, and then I sat with it a week, because that is not a description, that is a method. Nobody is that ordinary by accident.

speakers.name: Margaux Dell
speakers.comment: Some of us practise. You want the honest version, Detective? I am not sure anymore which one is the act, and the day I have to choose I would rather not be holding a warrant. Coffee is on me.

speakers.name: Margaux Dell
speakers.comment: You could have been rich twenty times over and instead you are chasing one page nobody will ever know you wrote. I front a desk for a living. I understand wanting the work to outlast the name.

speakers.name: Old Penny
speakers.comment: It is not the name I am after, it is the patina. Anybody can be rich, love. Very few can make a thing that has had time to settle. Sit — the ink is drying and I have got a kettle.

speakers.name: Old Penny
speakers.comment: You will find me eventually. I want you to know I have enjoyed the chase and I have done my best work because of it. A forger without an honest cop is just a man with good paper.

speakers.name: Detective Aria Voss
speakers.comment: That is the most annoying compliment I have ever been paid and I am keeping it. Do not slow down on my account. If I catch you sloppy, neither of us gets what we came for.

speakers.name: The Reanimation Counter's Best Work
speakers.comment: You put me on the runway three days after the accident and never once mentioned it. The stitching was visible. You lit it. Nobody else would have called that a choice.

speakers.name: Mortimer Vance
speakers.comment: It was the best line in the collection, darling, and the accident had nothing to do with it — the seam did. I do not stage tragedies. I stage structure. Stand up straight; you are a silhouette.

speakers.name: The Widow Marrowlace
speakers.comment: You speak of death as one speaks of weather, and I have carried mine a hundred years as though it were stone. I do not offer this as criticism. I offer it because I am tired of the stone.

speakers.name: Scustodian Bray
speakers.comment: Then set it down on my counter, love, and let us have a look at it. Nothing walks in here I have not seen before. A hundred years is a long while to hold anything without a receipt.

speakers.name: Hex the Necromancer
speakers.comment: Okay so — no, buddy, DOWN — so he was a returns problem three separate times, and each time the family came back for him, which is honestly our best retention number, and — BISCUIT. The rug.

speakers.name: Biscuit
speakers.comment: THE RUG IS MY FRIEND! THE RUG IS SOFT AND IT IS MY FRIEND AND I AM CHEWING IT BECAUSE I LOVE IT! YOU CAME BACK FOR ME THREE TIMES! I AM NEVER BEING RETURNED AGAIN!

speakers.name: Mortimer Vance
speakers.comment: The veil, madame, is the most disciplined tailoring in this city, and you have worn it a century without once letting it become a costume. I would kill for that restraint. I have, in fact.

speakers.name: The Widow Marrowlace
speakers.comment: I am aware of what you have done. I wear it because setting it aside would require me to decide something, and I have not decided. You may photograph it. You may not lift it.

speakers.name: The Outlaw Made of Dust
speakers.comment: Heard you preach. Good voice. Real good. Watched the collection plate after, and watched what walked out behind it. Ain't my business. Just want you knowin' somebody counted.

speakers.name: Reverend Two-Shadows
speakers.comment: Counting is a fine and Christian habit, friend, and I would never begrudge a man his arithmetic. Come back Sunday. Sit near the front where I can see you. The singing is worth the trip.

speakers.name: The Outlaw Made of Dust
speakers.comment: Spite and a sense of humor. Same mortar I'm held with. Canyon took somethin' off both of us and neither one went quiet about it. Ride easy, Annie. Or don't. Ain't my call.

speakers.name: Dust Annie
speakers.comment: Won't. Ain't ridden easy since. Nice to meet a fella held together by the same bad idea, though. Could count on one hand who I'd say that to. Got a hand and a half left.

speakers.name: The Ghost in the Saloon
speakers.comment: Big loud pile of somebody else's money, out here givin' it back. I'd call it noble but you'd get a head about it, and the head's already the size of a water tower.

speakers.name: The Iron Pacific
speakers.comment: WHOO-EEE! The spirit's got JOKES! Ain't nobility, ghost — it's INVENTORY! They built her to carry their gold and nobody wrote down where it had to GO! Climb aboard, I'll show you the ledger!

speakers.name: The Crossroads Coyote
speakers.comment: Two options, same as always. You could tell this town what you are and they'd thank you, or you could keep standin' there sayin' nothin' and they'd thank you anyway. Fair price either way.

speakers.name: Quiet Deputy Sull
speakers.comment: I will keep standing. The thanks is not the reason. There is a thing in the hills that counts how many of them there are. It has counted the same number for nine years.

speakers.name: Devorah Kell
speakers.comment: Penny, I want to say — genuinely — that your organizing is some of the best project work in this building. Which is why I have moved you to a team reporting directly to me. Congratulations.

speakers.name: Penny Wrecker
speakers.comment: Oh that is GOOD. That is really good. You put a promotion on it so I cannot call it retaliation. Fine. New team, new break room, same bylaws. See you at the meeting. Bring chairs.

speakers.name: The Many-Eyed Manager
speakers.comment: Employee designation pending. The document declines to be filed by anyone below director grade, which is either insubordination or excellent instinct. We have not determined which. We are not in a hurry.

speakers.name: The Form That Bites
speakers.comment: Clause 9(b) is unambiguous. Filing by an unauthorized party voids the instrument and, per subsection (iv), the party. This is not insubordination. It is the document performing correctly. Sign where indicated.

speakers.name: Penny Wrecker
speakers.comment: Here is what gets me — you are good at this. Genuinely good. Every clause lands, every smile hits, and you could have spent all that on something that was not keeping four hundred people mildly scared.

speakers.name: Devorah Kell
speakers.comment: Mildly is doing a great deal of work in that sentence and I appreciate the precision. I do think about it. Usually on Sundays. Then Monday arrives and the building still needs running.

speakers.name: Penny Wrecker
speakers.comment: Old man has been holding the line since before I could spell bylaw, and he did it without a single slogan. I bring the noise. He brings the part where the noise actually wins.

speakers.name: Grub
speakers.comment: Slogans wear out, kid. Bylaws don't. You bring 'em loud and I'll bring 'em legal, and between us the boss finds out he can't get good help cheap no more. Sit down. Eat somethin'.

speakers.name: Inkwell
speakers.comment: SHE'S GOT A ROOM! She's got a room and a menu and a whole — folks, the refreshments are POISONED and she TELLS you, that's the bit, that's the whole bit, and I am OBSESSED.

speakers.name: Madame Luxoria
speakers.comment: You are very loud and very correct, and I find I do not mind either. Telling them is the courtesy. A guest who drinks knowing is a guest who has chosen. Do sit. The red one is fine.

speakers.name: The Understudy for the Final Boss
speakers.comment: You run a dungeon where nobody dies, which — sorry — which means there is no final boss, which means I would have nothing to understudy, and I have been thinking about that a lot. Is there a job?

speakers.name: Grenidan
speakers.comment: There is always a job. Front desk needs covering Thursdays and the goblins would like somebody who does not flinch. It is not menacing work. Honestly, that is the pitch. Dental after ninety days.

speakers.name: The Big Bad Who Lost a Bet
speakers.comment: I ended a world once and now I make soup for a woman who beat me at cards, so hear me: the dramatic plan is not the part that matters. Ask what you WANT. Ghastly question. Ask it.

speakers.name: Vexa Thornes
speakers.comment: I have a monologue about that, actually, it is six minutes and it builds beautifully and it — it does not answer the question. Does it. ...No. It does not. Damn. How is the soup.

items.title: The Ringmaster of the Tent That Wasn't There Yesterday

speakers.name: The Aerialist With No Wire
speakers.comment: There is nothing under me. There was nothing under me last night in a different town. The tent moves and the drop does not change. I have stopped asking which of those you arranged.

speakers.name: The Ringmaster of the Tent That Wasn't There Yesterday
speakers.comment: Ohhh, but the ASKING was the good part! Ladies and gentlemen, she has stopped asking! No, no — stay up there, my dear. The tent goes where the story is not finished, and yours is a long way off.

speakers.name: The Aerialist With No Wire
speakers.comment: You land. Every time, you land. I do not, yet, and I watch you to learn how. Three seconds, four. Tell me what you gave them for it, and whether it was worth the landing.

speakers.name: Pirouette
speakers.comment: I do not know what I gave. That is the trouble — you never see the price at the time, you only notice one day that you are lighter than you were. Come down when you can. I will hold the ladder.

speakers.name: The Conductor's Ghost
speakers.comment: You are playing his ending and he never wrote one. Forgive me — I reach for the baton and there is no — I only mean that an unfinished phrase is not a wound. Some of us simply stop.

speakers.name: Maestro Clank
speakers.comment: Then I shall stop for him, and not before. The dissonance is not grief, sir. The dissonance is a held note with nobody left to release it. I will hold it. It is what I am for.
